beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Living Research Book proposes a different unit for communicating an evolving research programme.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its starting point is that scientific work already exceeds the articles describing it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Claims depend on datasets, code, decisions, failures, and knowledge scattered across separate records.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The distinctive proposal separates evidence records while presenting a coherent, versioned intellectual account.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This is an institutional design to investigate, not a prediction that longer publications automatically improve science.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers can examine how maintained knowledge might support explanation, review, credit, and selective disclosure.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book begins with a mismatch between research activity and its conventional public account.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Evidence, code, decisions, and revisions develop across many separate working materials.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An article can describe an important result without preserving every dependency needed for reuse.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Later readers and reviewers must reconstruct connections that the research team once understood.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposal asks whether that reconstruction burden can be reduced systematically.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This is why its subject is a maintained research institution, not simply a longer manuscript.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book considers a future built from smaller claims, datasets, and executable objects.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Those components support precise reuse but do not automatically provide a coherent explanation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its proposal keeps separate evidence records underneath a sustained intellectual account.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers could follow the argument while inspecting the dependencies relevant to a particular question.
